To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We present a multi person pose estimation system that outperforms the state of the Art by a large margin.

(1) bottom up proposals for parts can significantly improve the performance of multi person pose estimation; (2) image conditioned pairwise terms are essential for the performance of multi-person pose estimation; (3) the proposed incremental optimization strategy is able to explore the space of solutions efficiently and thus leads to both better performance and faster inference times.
(i) a bottom up approach is more robust to occlusion and (ii) a novel image conditioned pairwise term is a better choice than an image independent one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the task of estimating human body poses in still images.
the problem of estimating the 3D pose of a human in a single image.
the problem of multi-person pose estimation, which is a fundamental problem in computer vision with a broad range of applications.

we propose a new multi person pose estimation approach which is both faster and more accurate.

The main takeaway from our work is that
by carefully combining the bottom up and top down paradigms, it is possible to achieve a better multi person pose estimation performance than either of these paradigms alone.
the problem of multi person pose estimation is not simply a matter of extending existing single person pose estimation methods to multiple people.
by leveraging the information from multiple people, we can achieve significant performance improvements on the challenging task of multi person pose estimation.
